thread_title: S. flava var. maxima Montgomery Co, NC
breadcrumb: S. flava var. maxima Montgomery Co, NC

posts.body_html:
These S. flava var. maximas originate from a hilly habitat, which is unusual for flavas since they normally are found in coastal, lowland savannah bogs. These have also been consistently yellow, at least outdoors here in Northern California.

Generally speaking, while flava var. flava is abundant in cultivation, flavas from this particular site are just starting to enter cultivation as far as I know: these genotypes are quite unique and so far, they're pretty easy to grow! Other flava var. flavas like the ones from Brunswick Co, NC can be a bit more challenging to cultivate since they're so dang rot prone!


The maximas from this population are pretty darn amazingly Yellow! Pics taken mostly on 5/19/23:






Holy Mole-ay!

posts.body_html:
Got some good pics of this clone, I have labeled it and now it will be individually propagated. This clone has consistently turned very yellow year after year and is for sure a winner! Pics taken 5/1/25:


SOOOOOO yellow!!!!




In their native hilly habitat, they probably don't color up like this because they don't get full sun (they grow in a slightly forested area), but here, they get sun from sun up till sunset!
